name: Gnanapureeswarar Temple, Tirunaalur Mayanam
deity: Shiva as Gnanapureeswarar (Gnanaparameswarar, Palasavanesar), with the goddess Gnanambikai (Periyanayagi)
tradition: Shaiva — a Paadal Petra Sthalam (a Mayana Kovil)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirunaalur Mayanam, near Kudavasal, honours Shiva as Gnanapureeswarar — the lord of the city of wisdom — with the goddess Gnanambikai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, it is counted among the sacred Mayana Kovils, the shrines associated with the cremation ground, where Shiva is worshipped as the lord who grants liberation beyond death.

sections.history: Tirunaalur Mayanam lies about 3 km from Kudavasal and some 17 km from Kumbakonam, in the Kudavasal taluk of Thanjavur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The suffix Mayanam marks it as a mayana kovil — one of the small group of temples in Shaiva literature associated with the cremation ground — and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Gnanapureeswarar — also Gnanaparameswarar and Palasavanesar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Gnanambikai, also Periyanayagi, in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. As a mayana kovil the temple carries the quiet gravity of a place that faces death and the grace beyond it.
sections.legends: The lord's name Gnanapureeswarar, 'lord of the city of knowledge,' and the goddess Gnanambikai, 'mother of wisdom,' make this a shrine of jnana, of saving knowledge. Its character as a mayana kovil — a temple of the cremation ground — recalls Shiva as the lord who dances in the burning-ground and grants release from the round of birth and death; here that mystery is softened into the grace of wisdom. As with many smaller delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana is kept in the local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine near Kudavasal. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail include Tirunaalur Mayanam among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirunaalur Mayanam the pilgrim comes to a mayana kovil, a shrine that faces mortality with the calm of wisdom. Before Gnanapureeswarar, lord of the city of knowledge, and Gnanambikai, mother of wisdom, the visitor finds the deep, quiet grace of a Tevaram temple where death is met by the saving knowledge of Shiva.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirunaalur Mayanam is about 3 km from Kudavasal and 17 km from Kumbakonam, in the Kudavasal taluk of Thanjavur district. Kudavasal and Kumbakonam are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
